title: Internal: handling procedure for refunding an excess withdrawal fee charged on a certificate funding transfer
content:
## Situation and policy

This policy governs an excess withdrawal fee charged on a Savings & Money Market Accounts account for the internal transfer by which the owner opened a certificate of deposit. Such a fee was assessed contrary to the charter and is refunded in full on the bank-error ground.

- The refund is one refund entry that names the fee being refunded, recorded as a refund of an excess withdrawal fee, with the ground "bank error".
- It posts on the business day it is made, which is the day of the contact when that is a business day and otherwise the next business day, and its statement cycle is the statement cycle that contains that posted date.
- A bank-error refund has no time limit and does not count toward the courtesy limit.

## Business effect

One refund credit posts, naming the excess withdrawal fee it refunds and the ground for the refund. The account's current balance goes up by the refunded amount at once. The refund's posted date is the business day it posts: the current date when that is a business day (Monday through Friday, other than a Federal Reserve holiday), otherwise the next business day. The refund then shows in the account's activity next to the fee.

## How it is invoked

The tool is refund_savings_withdrawal_fee_774e6cc0. It is an internal tool that must first be unlocked (unlock) and then called (call) by the agent.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format or allowed values |
|---|---|---|
| savings_account_id | the reference number of the savings or money market account that was charged, as returned by the savings account lookup | identifier |
| customer_id | the customer reference number of the account owner, as returned by the customer profile lookup | identifier |
| source_item_id | the reference number of the excess withdrawal fee entry being refunded, as returned by the savings activity lookup | identifier |
| amount | the refunded amount | USD, 2 decimal places, always positive |
| adjustment_reason | the ground for the refund | exactly one of: courtesy_waiver (a goodwill refund of a fee that was charged correctly), bank_error (a refund of a fee that was charged contrary to the savings charter), none (not a refund ground; never used for a refund) |
| statement_cycle | the statement cycle in which the refund posts | YYYY-MM, the month in which the statement cycle that contains the refund's posted date closes |

The source_item_id is the fee entry, not the withdrawal the fee was attached to. The tool records the values it is given; it does not work out the amount or check eligibility.

## Return

A successful call returns:

- savings_txn_id: the reference number of the refund entry; a returned savings_txn_id means the refund posted;
- refunded_fee_id: the fee entry refunded;
- amount: USD with 2 decimal places;
- adjustment_reason: the ground recorded;
- posted_date: the business day the refund posted, YYYY-MM-DD;
- new_balance: the account's current balance after the refund, USD with 2 decimal places.

## Contract Q&A

**Which fee entries is this tool for?** Excess withdrawal fees only; the entry it posts is recorded as a refund of an excess withdrawal fee.

**Which cycle goes into statement_cycle?** The statement cycle that contains the refund's posted date. On a business day that is the cycle containing the current date; on a Saturday, Sunday or Federal Reserve holiday it is the cycle containing the next business day.
